definition: Non-human (also spelled nonhuman) is any entity displaying some, but not enough, human characteristics to be considered human.
details: The term has been used in a variety of contexts and may refer to objects that have been developed with human intelligence, such as robots or vehicles.

explainer.lead: Non-human describes an entity that has some human-like characteristics but not enough to be considered human. The term helps distinguish human-like features from human identity when discussing things such as robots and vehicles.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a toy robot that can talk and wave like a person. It acts a little like you, but that does not make it a person, so it can be called non-human. The word points out the similarities while still marking the difference.
tiers.practitioner: In engineering, non-human is a broad descriptive label rather than a technical specification. It can apply to robots or vehicles developed through human intelligence. When using it, identify the relevant human-like characteristics instead of treating the label as evidence of a particular capability or design.
tiers.paperLevel: An entity x is non-human when x displays some human characteristics H, but not enough of them to be classified as human. The definition specifies neither a required set of characteristics nor a threshold for classification. It also provides no measurement procedure.

explainer.example: A robot that can talk and respond to questions has some human-like characteristics. Those traits alone do not make it human, so it may be described as non-human.

usedIn.name: Robotics
usedIn.detail: Robots may display selected human-like characteristics while remaining non-human entities.

usedIn.name: Vehicles
usedIn.detail: Vehicles are among the human-developed objects to which the term may refer.

explainer.intuition: Resembling a person in some ways is not the same as being a person. Non-human marks that gap without requiring the entity to have any particular technical design.
howItWorks: Note any human-like characteristics it displays.
Judge that these characteristics are not enough to classify it as human.
Use non-human as a broad description, not a measure of capability.
explainer.whyItMatters: The term allows discussion of human-like features in objects without treating those features as proof of humanity. It is deliberately broad, so precise descriptions of the entity and its characteristics remain important.
misconceptions: Non-human does not mean completely lacking human-like characteristics.
The label does not, by itself, specify intelligence or technical sophistication.
Human-like behavior alone does not make an entity human.
